prop_desc: Constitutional amendment giving the General Assembly power to divide the state into a number of judicial districts and to provide for the election of one or more Superior Court judges for each district
notes_endorse: Editorial: 'On the whole we favor the amendment because we think it is necessary to bring the State out of the horse and buggy era and up to date in the important matter of the number of judges and their allocation.'

prop_desc: More adequate pay for members of the General Assembly ($15/day for 90 days for 170 legislators)
notes_endorse: Editorial 'Add: Amendments': 'we are for the amendments, all of them'

prop_desc: Amendment applying common-sense to judicial procedure at the request of the Judicial Council
notes_endorse: Editorial: 'we are quite willing to approve the recommendations of the Judicial Council'

prop_desc: Greater safeguarding of retirement trust funds for teachers and other state employees
notes_endorse: Editorial endorses 'protection of teacher and other state employees' retirement funds'

prop_desc: Amendment permitting any person, when represented by counsel, to waive indictment in all except capital cases
notes_endorse: Editorial 'Constitutional Amendments Needed': 'In the opinion of the Daily News all these proposed amendments are good and should pass.'

prop_desc: Amendment safeguarding the funds of the Teachers' and State Employees' Retirement Fund
notes_endorse: Editorial: 'all these proposed amendments are good and should pass.'

prop_desc: Amendment increasing the compensation of the members of the General Assembly
notes_endorse: Editorial: 'The third is needed to give the members of the Legislature a chance to break even on their stay in Raleigh.'

prop_desc: Amendment permitting the General Assembly to prescribe the number of regular Superior Court judges in each judicial district
notes_endorse: Editorial: 'all these proposed amendments are good and should pass.'

prop_desc: Constitutional amendment dealing with the assignment and jurisdiction of Superior Court judges; transfers power of assignment from Governor to Chief Justice of NC Supreme Court and gives Legislature power to define jurisdiction of special and emergency judges
notes_endorse: Editorial 'Amending Constitution': 'The Daily News is very much in favor of this amendment, which is overdue and which holds a good deal of promise for betterment of the whole judicial system of the State.'

prop_desc: Amendment transferring from the Governor to the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court the authority to assign judges to courts or call special terms, and to give the Legislature power to define the jurisdiction of special judges
notes_endorse: Editorial: 'all these proposed amendments are good and should pass.'

prop_desc: Amendment to enable counties to raise tax rates by raising the limit from 15 cents to 20 cents on the $100 valuation of total state and county tax
notes_endorse: Editorial 'Three N.C. Amendments': 'On the whole we expect that the amendment is needed.'

prop_desc: Amendment providing for filling vacancies in the General Assembly by gubernatorial appointment upon recommendation of executive committees of party and county
notes_endorse: Editorial: 'This amendment seems to provide a reasonable method of filling vacancies in the Legislature.'

prop_desc: Amendment empowering the Governor to fill vacancies occurring in the Judicial Department when impossible to get an election in time
notes_endorse: Editorial: 'This also seems to be a reasonable means of filling a vacancy.'

prop_desc: Amendment that would limit each county to one state senator (kill the constitutional provision requiring senatorial districts to be changed after every US Census)
notes_endorse: Editorial 'Honoring The Constitution': 'The Daily News wholeheartedly advises a no vote.' Argues amendment would deny proper representation to growing cities.

prop_desc: Amendment allowing retired members of the State Supreme Court to be called back for emergency duty on the high court bench
notes_endorse: Editorial 'Those Other Amendments': 'We favor it.'

prop_desc: Amendment to establish a board of paroles with complete authority to grant, revoke and terminate paroles, transferring burden of paroles from Governor to parole board
notes_endorse: Editorial: 'We favor the amendment.'

prop_desc: Senatorial limitation amendment (one senator per county)
notes_endorse: Editorial: 'the notorious senatorial limitation amendment which we have discussed in detail in other editorials, and which we oppose.'

prop_desc: Senatorial limitation amendment - characterized by editorial as 'more gerrymandering' that purposely lumps Democratic counties with Republican counties to water down GOP representation in Raleigh
notes_endorse: Editorial 'More Gerrymandering': 'They can vote against Constitutional Amendment Three on Tuesday.'

prop_desc: Amendment to reduce the length of residence for voting in a precinct from four months to 30 days preceding an election
notes_endorse: Editorial: 'That is a sensible change, and we favor it.'

prop_desc: Amendment to abolish requirement for an election for short term offices occurring between the date of the general election and the following January 1, allowing Governor's appointee to serve until the January 1 following the next general election
notes_endorse: Editorial: 'This eliminates confusion. We favor it.'

prop_desc: Greensboro fluoridation of city water supply
notes_endorse: Editorial 'Evidence On Fluoridation': 'Therefore, guided by reason, we favor its use in Greensboro.'

prop_desc: Constitutional amendment which would raise jurisdiction of justices of the peace from $50 to $200 in civil matters
notes_endorse: Editorial 'Democracy In Action': 'opposition to the constitutional amendment which would raise jurisdiction of justices of the peace... We do not favor increased responsibility for magistrates until overdue reforms are effected.'

prop_desc: Greensboro fluoridation referendum (second time in four years)
notes_endorse: Editorial 'Fluoridation And Tomorrow's Election': 'The Daily News stands on the side of most of the nation's reputable doctors and dentists.' Endorses fluoridation.

prop_desc: Court Improvement constitutional amendment - reform of NC court system, including changes to magistrate/justice of peace system
notes_endorse: Editorial 'Court Improvement: The People's Prerogative': discusses court improvement amendment, with the paper appearing to support it (image too small to read with full confidence). Notes 'The issue is now up to the people.'

prop_desc: School Bonds - $100 million school bond issue for North Carolina (3,142 public school facilities, etc.)
notes_endorse: Editorial 'School Bonds: Need And Reason': supports school bond issue, arguing 'There can be no question of school bonds' for educational improvement.

prop_desc: 1970 NC bond issues (multiple state bonds, including likely highway, prison, mental health, education)
notes_endorse: Editorial 'Bonds: a sound investment' endorses NC bond issues. Image too small to read details but title clearly indicates endorsement.

prop_desc: NC Constitutional Amendment 1
notes_endorse: Editorial 'Amendments: a reminder': 'We recommend a vote FOR amendments one, four, five, six and seven, and a vote AGAINST amendments two and three.'

prop_desc: Executive reorganization amendment - could open the way to executive tampering with higher education
notes_endorse: Editorial: 'in our view ought to be deferred until the General Assembly clarifies it.' Vote AGAINST.

prop_desc: Amendment allowing self-summoning legislative session (instead of Governor summoning special sessions)
notes_endorse: Editorial: 'we see no compelling reason why the traditional practice of having the Governor summon special sessions of the General Assembly should not be continued.' Vote AGAINST.

prop_desc: NC Constitutional Amendment 4
notes_endorse: Editorial: 'Amendments one and four through seven, inclusive, are sound and should be passed.' Vote FOR.

prop_desc: NC Constitutional Amendment 5
notes_endorse: Editorial: 'sound and should be passed.' Vote FOR.

prop_desc: NC Constitutional Amendment 6
notes_endorse: Editorial: 'sound and should be passed.' Vote FOR.

prop_desc: NC Constitutional Amendment 7
notes_endorse: Editorial: 'sound and should be passed.' Vote FOR.

prop_desc: Amendment with two main provisions: (1) constitutional change to lower voting age to 18 (already secured by federal legislation), and (2) age limits for state offices
notes_endorse: Editorial 'Five constitutional matters': 'amendment should fail.' Part one is essentially unnecessary; part two would bar 18-year-olds from state office and is patently discriminatory. 'This amendment, too, should fail.'

prop_desc: Judicial amendment imposing mandatory age limit on state judges - ceiling on appellate judges of 72 years and bar to several pres ent justices of Supreme Court from ever becoming chief justice
notes_endorse: Editorial: 'in our opinion, should be voted down.' Lumps together two limitations.

prop_desc: Judicial amendment to create disciplinary machinery for the removal and censure of state judges; subjects judges to removal in general elections and to removal for bodily or mental incapacity by General Assembly
notes_endorse: Editorial: 'we see no case for adding a third means of discipline or deposition. This amendment should fail.'

prop_desc: Environmental Protection Amendment sponsored by Sen. Hargrove (Skipper) Bowles - constitutional preservation of state's natural environment, water, air, open lands, parks, streams and rivers
notes_endorse: Editorial: 'Unquestionably the most important is Amendment Four, the so-called Environmental Protection Amendment. The voters should endorse it with enthusiasm.'

prop_desc: Amendment prohibiting the incorporation of new towns or cities in close proximity to existing cities (anti-incorporation amendment)
notes_endorse: Editorial: 'The amendment deserves a favorable vote.'

prop_desc: NC constitutional amendment to require state's judges be lawyers. Editorial 'For lawyers as judges' urges affirmative vote on this referendum: 'It is time we claimed that assurance for the citizens of this state. An affirmative vote on this question will not guarantee that we will get wise judges, but it will give us judges who know the law.'
Constitutional amendment providing that the term of office of members of the General Assembly begins on the first day of January following their election. Editorial recommends voting (For).
Constitutional amendment permitting the issuance of tax increment bonds without voter approval. Editorial recommends voting (For).
